Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
Experience in creating, implementing, and publicizing diverse, successful, mostly low-budget large-and small-scale events.
Experience with advising, especially to college-age students; experience working with student organizations and campus departments and committees.
Experience working with diverse student populations, particularly with LGBTQIA2S+ students.
Experience in website creation or content management.
Related administrative experience sufficient to provide support functions to the Resource Center Director and staff.
Knowledge and experience using standard office computer applications such as Google Email and Calendars, Word, Excel, database software.

Under the general supervision of the Lionel Cantú Queer Resource Center ('the Cantú') Director, the Cantú Program Coordinator provides programmatic, administrative, and facilities support to advance the mission of the Lionel Cantú Queer Resource Center and the broader Resource Centers organization. Under the general supervision of the Cantú Director, the Coordinator plans, implements, and assesses co-curricular programs that support LGBTQIA+ students, with particular attention to QTBIPOC and historically excluded student communities. Responsibilities include coordinating large-scale and recurring programs; supervising and advising undergraduate and graduate student staff; providing fiscal and administrative support (including purchasing, reimbursements, reservations, and data tracking); and supporting collaborative programming across Resource Centers.

This position also provides facilities coordination for three Resource Centers locations, the Cantú Queer Center, Crown College House, and Cardiff House, by managing space reservations, submitting CruzFix and facilities work orders, coordinating with campus partners, supporting safety and accessibility needs, and ensuring shared spaces are functional and welcoming. The Coordinator serves as a key operational connector across centers, supporting cross-unit initiatives, shared events, and day-to-day continuity of services.
Abilities in initiative and resourcefulness.
Critical Race and Ethnic Studies.

Feminist/Gender/Sexuality Studies.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.

The selected candidate will be required to work primarily on campus, with periods of remote work possible based on operational needs. If a hybrid work schedule is confirmed, the selected candidate must be able to work successfully from a home/remote office and be able to fulfill the requirements of the UCSC telecommuting agreement.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

The University of California has implemented a Vaccination Policy covering all employees. Employees, including new hires, are required to comply with any applicable policies relating to the University of California vaccine program.

Per the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA), this position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter. The selected candidate will be required to report known or suspected child abuse or neglect as defined by CANRA and will be required to sign a Statement Acknowledging Requirement to Report Child Abuse prior to commencing employment. CANRA Penal Codes, and related definitions, requirements, and responsibilities may be obtained here.
Ability to solve problems.
Ability to work overtime including evenings, nights, weekends and holidays to meet operational needs, and work an alternate work schedule shift as required.
Organization skills and abilities sufficient to independently establish priorities and complete concurrent assignments with frequent interruptions and noisy work environment.
Ability to maintain appearance and conduct suitable for working in a professional setting.
Strong cultural competency skills to engage with individuals from diverse backgrounds, particularly those with identities served by this Resource Center.
Knowledge/understanding of diversity issues in higher education, trauma-informed practices, and queer pedagogies, particularly related to LGBTQIA2S+ communities.

Interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to give, receive and record clear, concise information or directions (written and oral), facilitate discussions, and mediate conflict resolutions.
Ability to exercise tact and diplomacy, sensitivity and helpfulness when interacting with students, faculty and staff from diverse cultural or socio-economic backgrounds or handling sensitive issues.
Ability to produce detailed reports and documents; ability to analyze data, present findings, and suggest resolutions.
Ability to learn policies and procedures from both verbal and written sources; ability to apply and explain office policies and procedures with consistency.
